cells.tense: You're in it right now, and you're not rushing it.
cells.verb: feeling your way forward into what hasn't happened yet, with your eyes open
cells.place: on a stretch of road where you can see the next step and nothing past it
cells.ask: Pick the one pull that actually moves you and keep showing up to it, steadily, without needing to know where it ends — and the picturing starts to come from what you've really lived.
cells.core:
You're in it right now, and you're not rushing it. You can feel your way forward into what hasn't happened yet with your eyes open, and you're doing it on a stretch of road where you can see the next step and nothing past it. You're not forcing the fog to clear. Each step is showing you the one after, and you're letting it.

That's working. If you want to give it somewhere to go: pick the one pull that actually moves you and keep showing up to it, steadily, without needing to know where it ends. The feeling becomes direction, and the picturing starts to come from what you've really lived.
cells.sheetLine: You can take the next step without seeing the road, and you're taking it.

cells.tense: You're living somewhere ahead of yourself, and it hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: feeling every possible future at full volume before any of them is real
cells.place: on a stretch of road you can't see the end of
cells.ask: Tend one real thing — a plant, a meal, a room — and let it grow at its own pace, without pulling at it — and the pictures start to come from what you've actually lived, not from what might.
cells.core:
You're living somewhere ahead of yourself, and it hasn't arrived. You're feeling every possible future at full volume before any of them is real, standing on a stretch of road you can't see the end of. The not-knowing was supposed to be room to walk in; it's become a flood of everything that might happen, all felt at once.

What you're reaching for is hard to hold. Here's a smaller thing: tend one real thing — a plant, a meal, a room — and let it grow at its own pace, without pulling at it. Something in front of you, growing slowly, gives the feeling-ahead a floor. And the pictures start to come from what you've actually lived, not from what might.
cells.sheetLine: You're feeling futures that haven't happened, all of them, at once.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: no longer letting yourself feel what might be coming
cells.place: on a stretch of road you can't see the end of
cells.ask: Ask one real question about what's actually in front of you, and let yourself not know the answer while you listen — and the picturing begins to come from what you've lived, including this.
cells.core:
You're still standing at a door that's already behind you. You've stopped letting yourself feel what might be coming, and you're standing on a stretch of road you can't see the end of as if you already know how it goes. You're reading this unknown off the last one. The wonder didn't fail you; it got set down, and the next step hasn't been taken.

I wouldn't push you to feel your way forward again — that's the empty part. Try this instead: ask one real question about what's actually in front of you, and let yourself not know the answer while you listen. Curiosity pulls the feeling back behind it. And the picturing begins to come from what you've lived, including this.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped feeling ahead, and you're calling it knowing.

cells.tense: You're already steering, with the pen down.
cells.verb: feeling your way through what's unclear and letting it guide you
cells.place: on a stretch of road you can't see the end of
cells.ask: Write down what you actually sense about where this goes, in plain sentences, once a day for a week, and check them against what happens — and the picturing becomes yours, coming from what you've lived.
cells.core:
You're already steering, with the pen down. You're feeling your way through what's unclear and letting it guide you, right here on a stretch of road you can't see the end of — and you'd say you have no idea, that you're just waiting to see. But the turns you're taking aren't random. Something in you is reading the fog, and it's good at it. You just don't call it yours.

A way to find out: write down what you actually sense about where this goes, in plain sentences, once a day for a week, and check them against what happens. Not to be right — to see whose hand is on the wheel. And the picturing becomes yours, coming from what you've lived.
cells.sheetLine: Your gut is already reading this. You're calling it waiting.
